questions.question: Driving involves risk. It is wise to keep improving your driving and observation skills.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Unsafe driving happens when drivers think they have nothing to improve. Always work to improve your driving and observation skills for your safety and the safety of others.

questions.question: If railroad crossing gates are down and red lights are flashing, you should:

options.text: Stop and proceed only when the gates are raised and the lights have stopped flashing.
Drive around the gates after stopping.
Drive side by side with the train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and proceed only when the gates are raised and the lights have stopped flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when warning lights flash and the gate lowers. Stay stopped until the gate raises and the lights stop flashing. Never drive around lowered gates. It is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians and frighten them so they'll think twice before crossing against a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians and cars in the intersection, even when you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. You should:

options.text: Sound your horn and maintain your speed.
Speed up to clear the area quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: This white sign means:

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Continue at your regular speed.
Look, listen, and prepare to stop at the crossing if necessary.
Stop at the railroad tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and prepare to stop at the crossing if necessary.
questions.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing, look, listen, slow down, and prepare to stop. Let any trains pass before you cross.

questions.question: To prevent yourself from becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Relax and concentrate on driving.
Drive above the posted speed limit.
Tailgate the driver in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and concentrate on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, focus on driving and don't take the actions of other drivers personally. Be realistic about travel time, drive at posted speeds, and forgive other drivers on the road.

questions.question: Which factor commonly contributes to traffic crashes?

options.text: Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions.
Getting adequate rest and staying alert.
Scanning the environment and staying focused on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving above the speed limit and driving too fast for conditions commonly cause accidents. Always drive with traffic flow and within legal speed limits.

questions.question: Changing lanes is best done:

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Gradually and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes gradually and carefully. Only change lanes when necessary. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: Directed to do so by a flagger.
It is controlled by a stop sign.
Flashing red signals and gates are present and operating.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign directs you to stop, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. You should:

options.text: Not think much about it because all vehicles are the same.
Hide from your friend that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore obvious defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes before driving to learn where all the vehicle's equipment is and how it works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes before driving to learn where all the vehicle's equipment is and how it works.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to find and understand the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any defects before driving.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to get out of an aggressive driver's way. Never compete with other drivers. This helps prevent crashes and keeps everyone safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at a steady red light. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if no sign says otherwise.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver cuts you off in traffic?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off in return.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go.
questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely. This helps prevent road rage and accidents.

questions.question: What does flashing amber lights on a school bus mean?

options.text: The driver is changing gears.
The bus will soon stop to pick up or drop off students.
The driver is about to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bus will soon stop to pick up or drop off students.
questions.explanation: Flashing amber lights warn you that the bus will soon stop. Slow down to 20 mph or less and be ready to stop. Do not pass a school bus with flashing amber lights.

questions.question: What is a result of driving too fast?

options.text: You save time and get there faster.
You can move around obstacles more easily.
It increases the risk of serious injury or death.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of serious injury or death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. Driving too fast does not save time and leads to poor driving decisions.

questions.question: What must you do if a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone?

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other drivers are doing instead of following the flagger.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws instead of the flagger's directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the flagger's directions.
questions.explanation: You must follow a flagger's directions in construction zones. Not obeying a flagger is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and drink alcohol before driving?

options.text: Nothing will happen.
You will be more alert.
You may not be able to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be able to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair your driving. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabilities. Only vehicles with disability license plates or placards may park there.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel drowsy while driving?

options.text: Try to stay awake.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: Stop at the nearest rest area to nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine and energy drinks do not replace real rest and may make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: Why should you not follow another car too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front suddenly slows or stops.
You may not see the turn signals.
You may not see the brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front suddenly slows or stops.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, you will not have enough time to stop if the car in front of you slows down or stops suddenly. This can cause a collision.

questions.question: What do highway markings do?

options.text: They are usually not important.
They are only found in construction zones.
They give information to drivers.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give information to drivers.
questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers. They show where to position your vehicle, tell you where it is safe to pass, and warn you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if the red lights are flashing, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is close. If you are not sure a train is far enough away, stop. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask you for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red warning lights are flashing or the gate is down, you must stop 15 to 50 feet from the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
The road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers right ahead. This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when it rains.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road ahead is closed to traffic.
Road work or maintenance is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road work or maintenance is ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction and maintenance signs are orange. They tell drivers about unusual or dangerous conditions in work zones. This sign warns you that construction is coming and you should slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: Before you change lanes or pass another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before moving your vehicle left or right to warn other drivers. Check your mirrors and turn your head to see your blind spot before you move your vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat if the vehicle has airbags.
An airbag can hurt an infant or small child, even in a slow crash.
Make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before driving, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chances of being hurt or killed in a crash. Children 12 and under should sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never put a rear-facing infant car seat in the front seat if there is a front airbag.

questions.question: When a blind or partially blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane crosses the street, what must you do?

options.text: You must always give them the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only need to give them the right-of-way at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must always give the right-of-way to anyone using a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: A police car, tow truck, or utility vehicle is parked on the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop abruptly.
Continue as usual.
Change lanes if you can and slow down as you pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes if you can and slow down as you pass.
questions.explanation: When you see a parked police car, tow truck, or other vehicle with flashing lights, move to another lane if possible to give it space. If you cannot change lanes, slow down as you pass.

questions.question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:

options.text: Always know the risks they are taking.
Cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
Drive better because they are more careful than sober drivers.
React faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and body. It makes judgment worse, blurs vision, reduces focus, and slows reaction time. It is never safe to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:

options.text: Make both substances weaker.
Make both substances stronger.
Help cure your illness.
Make you a better driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make both substances stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs makes both effects stronger. Driving after alcohol alone is dangerous. Driving after drugs alone is dangerous. Driving after mixing them is even more dangerous.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers:

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
An intersection is coming.
Road construction is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane is ending. All traffic in the right lane must move left into another lane.

questions.question: You hear a siren from an emergency vehicle behind you. You should:

options.text: Stop right where you are.
Pull to the right and stop.
Speed up to move out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, slow down and safely move to the right side of the road and stop. Clear the path for the emergency vehicle. If traffic is heavy and you cannot move right, keep going slowly until you find a safe place to pull over.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The first driver to arrive has the right-of-way.
The last driver to arrive has the right-of-way.
One driver can drive through without stopping.
One driver waves the others to go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first driver to arrive has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: All vehicles must stop at a four-way stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the left gives way to the driver on the right.
